title: China joins the World Trade Organization
summary: After 15 years of negotiations, WTO members approved the terms of China's accession on 10 November 2001 at the Fourth Ministerial Conference in Doha, Qatar. China signed the next day and became the WTO's 143rd member on 11 December 2001, taking on commitments to open its trade regime. China's economy, the world's sixth largest in 2001, was four times larger by 2018, and China had become the largest goods trader among WTO members, though US officials argued it kept much of its state-led system.

uncertainty.note: WTO Ministerial Conference approved entry on 10 November 2001 in Doha; accession took effect 30 days after ratification on 11 December 2001.

beats.caption: The Fourth WTO Ministerial Conference in Doha approves China's terms of accession.
China formally enters the WTO as its 143rd member, catalyzing rapid industrial export growth and supply chain integration.

related.because: China applied to resume its status under GATT in 1986, creating the framework that culminated in its WTO accession.
Deng Xiaoping's domestic economic reforms enabled China to liberalize trade and meet multilateral WTO entry criteria.
